Canada is apparently the enemy now, while North Korea gets upgraded to global bestie. Welcome to another countdown of funniest AI political satire, where this week's headlines have already done most of the comedy writers' work for them.

Come for the politics, stay for the escalating absurdity--and see which clips made it all the way to the top.

**" Why are people moving to Bridgeport, CT?"**
The pitch was waterfront views, beaches, food, entertainment and easy train access to New York City. The post also noted that more buyers moving from NYC are adding Bridgeport to their home searches.
And it upset me.
Not because I have anything against the realtor. And certainly not because I don't want people moving to Bridgeport.
**I want people investing in Bridgeport. I want businesses opening here. I want property values rising. I want people to look at Bridgeport and see tremendous opportunity.**
What upset me was what that post unintentionally represents.
After decades of one-party government, are we finally going to declare Bridgeport a success because people from New York discover they can afford to live here?
**What about the people who are already here?**
**Affordable to whom?**
Bridgeport families have been waiting for their brighter day.
* Waiting for better schools.
* Waiting for safer streets.
* Waiting for better-paying jobs.
* Waiting for pathways to homeownership.
* Waiting for government to deliver.

Now housing costs are already squeezing the people who stayed. DataHaven's 2025 Bridgeport Equity Report found **54% of Bridgeport renter households were housing-cost burdened** , while the state comptroller reported 58.7% for renters across the Greater Bridgeport planning area.
_And just this week, two new residential projects were approved near Park Avenue without designated affordable units._
* Development isn't the enemy.
* **Displacement is.**
* **Don 't force people out. Give them a way up.**

We shouldn't have to choose between a declining Bridgeport and a revitalized Bridgeport that its existing residents can no longer afford.
There is a third choice:
**Build a Bridgeport where the people who are here participate in its success.**
That means:
**Renting -> Earning -> Saving -> Owning.**
It means:
* Better schools and real educational choices.
* College for the students who want college and skilled trades for those who want another path.
* Attracting employers so that Bridgeport isn't merely someplace to sleep before catching a train to somebody else's economy.
* Creating pathways to homeownership, including affordable owned homes and apartments, so rising property values create generational wealth for Bridgeport families instead of becoming an eviction notice.

> Interestingly, Bridgeport's own Affordable Housing Plan says housing policy should provide options not merely for people coming to Bridgeport, but for those who **want to stay** , particularly young people.
**That 's the Bridgeport I want to fight for.**
**A Bridge to a Brighter Day**
Bridgeport isn't New York City.
And it shouldn't aspire to become somebody else's commuter town.
Its name tells us what it can be:
**A BRIDGE to a brighter day.**
**A PORT of opportunity for every child.**
A place where your ZIP code doesn't determine your future.
* Welcome the new family arriving from New York.
* Welcome the entrepreneur opening a business.
* Welcome the developer willing to invest.
* **But never abandon the people who were here first.**

I understand why people are frustrated.
**I 'm here to turn that frustration into action.**
And instead of asking, _" Why are people moving to Bridgeport?"_
I want us asking:
**" How do we make sure the people of Bridgeport can afford to stay, prosper, and own a piece of its future?"**
**Michael Goldstein for Congress**
_People Over Parties._
_Put a Doctor in the House._
_Paid for by Michael Goldstein for Congress._

| | | | | | | | | | | | **Saturday Evening “Doctors for Tessa” Event** Doctors for Tessa is a campaign fundraiser scheduled for Saturday, August 28, from 5-7 p.m. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker, Tessa knows how important it is to back healthcare workers. Join hosts Dr. Stephanie Bolton, Dr. Cameo Carter, and Dr. Alex Moreland for this informative and fun event. Scan the QR code below or [click here to RSVP today on Act Blue](https://us.list-manage.com/BdGYzym39Ig?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c) to receive the exact location.

# Endorsement Alerts
---
| | **National Security Leaders for America** “August 26, 2026 - National Security Leaders for America is proud to endorse Tessa Lynn Hodge for U.S. House of Representatives. As retired senior military leaders, diplomats, and national security professionals, we understand that leadership is ultimately a matter of character, judgment, service, and responsibility. Those qualities matter in every elected office...Tessa Lynn Hodge has earned our endorsement because she will bring those principles to the House of Representatives...National Security Leaders for America proudly endorses Tessa Lynn Hodge for the U.S. House of Representatives and encourages the voters of California’s 23rd Congressional District to vote for her on November 3rd.” [Read more here.](https://us.list-manage.com/mjeq7Cd834R?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c)
[](https://us.list-manage.com/lTmC9RljMqu?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c)
**Equality California Endorsement** Equality California endorses and supports 100% pro-equality candidates — up and down the ballot — fighting for LGBTQ+ civil rights, reproductive freedom and social justice. Tessa Lynn Hodge is their endorsed candidate for California’s 23rd Congressional District. [See more here](https://us.list-manage.com/k595Hizkjrn?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c).
---
[|

| | | | | | | | | | | |
**Join the Blue Wave Canvassing Team** Tessa Lynn Hodge’s team canvasses regularly in California’s District 23. Even during hot August, we’ve visited over 4000 homes. Events are scheduled in Victorville, Yucaipa, Apple Valley, Hesperia, Loma Linda, and all over the district with our Create Your Own Canvassing Events. These canvassing events are designed by YOU! You decide when, where, and whether or not you want to talk to voters. We’ll supply literature, a walking list of progressive voters, and even extra volunteers for your event. Let’s get out the vote by letting folks in your neighborhood know about Tessa’s priorities for California 23.
[Check out the details and sign up here](https://us.list-manage.com/xFmMSBp89kN?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c). You can also get to the sign up at [tessaforca.com](https://us.list-manage.com/ZoG4FgNBpSs?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c) and click on _Knock Door With Us!_
---
| | **Countdown to the Election** Election Day is November 3, 2026. That is just 67 days away! Remember to encourage your family and friends to vote. Tell them voter registration ends October 19, 2026. ([Conditional registration](https://us.list-manage.com/yvtwRo6rdPV?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c) may be available for those who miss that day.) [You can check your Voter Status here.](https://us.list-manage.com/kpehvLyk8E_?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c)

---
| | Friends, THANK YOU for being the best part of this campaign. We are a people-powered campaign, and I love hearing from you—the people in my community.
As November 3 approaches, we have just 67 more days to help our family, neighbors, and friends commit to vote in order to prioritize the well-being of people over party differences. I[ encourage you to go to my Issues page and remind yourself of what I stand for.](https://us.list-manage.com/jRz365NmvnF?e=db7cb92046&c2id=f83d0f9d6921da6906ad40d7e682269c) We can bring these priorities to CA-23. With gratitude and determination,

body:
YOU DID IT — THANK YOU!

| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | Dear Peter,
**YOU DID IT — THANK YOU!**
When we told you that our campaign needed help purchasing more signs, **you stepped up.**
Because of your generosity, **we were able to order additional Enoch for Congress signs, and they are now on the way!**
That is what grassroots support looks like. You saw a need, you responded, and together we were able to get it done.
**Now, we need your help with the next critical phase of the campaign.**

### WE'RE ALMOST OUT OF LITERATURE
Our volunteers have been working hard — canvassing neighborhoods, attending community events, talking with voters, and distributing campaign literature.
As a result, **we are almost out of literature again.**
We need to place another order on Monday, so that our volunteers don't run out of the materials they need to introduce our campaign to voters.And that's not our only upcoming expense.

### VOTING BEGINS OCTOBER 6
We have just over a month before voters begin casting their ballots.Between now and then, we need to dramatically increase the number of voters we are reaching across Ohio's 8th Congressional District.
Our next round of fundraising will help us:**✓ Print thousands of additional pieces of campaign literature****✓ Purchase postcards to reach voters directly in their homes****✓ Prepare for additional campaign sign needs****✓ Launch our digital advertising campaign****✓ Expand voter outreach and Get Out the Vote efforts**
This is when the campaign begins to accelerate.
We need voters seeing our signs throughout their communities.We need volunteers carrying our literature door to door.We need postcards arriving in voters' mailboxes.And soon, we need our digital ads reaching voters online.
**We have the organization. Now we need the resources to reach as many voters as possible.**

### CAN YOU HELP US FUND THE NEXT ROUND?

Once voting begins on **October 6** , the race changes.People will no longer simply be deciding how they might vote.
**They will be casting their ballots.**

I don't agree with Speaker Mike Johnson very often. But he's right about one thing. When he came to Southwest Washington last month to raise money for my opponent, he told the room that Washington's 3rd District will decide who controls the House. He's right. name: Tom Fitton
subject: Supreme Court Urged to Protect Access to Voter Rolls
body:
Obama’s ‘Diaper Disparity’ Program Gets $29 Million

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH URGES SUPREME COURT TO PROTECT PUBLIC ACCESS TO STATE
VOTER ROLLS

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38577&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS8zN3M1dXFCWFFzND91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=5554c567b258164fe04bab4c6f07859eab01904dbf14596821039facc410b613]

We continue to insist that dirty voter rolls can mean dirty elections.
We are again taking up the fight for clean elections by asking the
Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) to make it clear that the
public has a right to see states’ voter registration lists.

We filed an _amicus curiae_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38571&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3B1YmxpYy1pbnRlcmVzdC1sZWdhbC12LW5hZ28taGF3YWlpLWVsZWN0aW9uLWFtaWN1cy05OC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=8df72eda1dde436b2698d382f27eb264aa9ce3df1af40230030a71b0afb192b3]
(friend of the court) brief to the Supreme Court supporting the Public
Interest Legal Foundation’s (PILF) petition for review of a Ninth
Circuit decision that allows Hawaii to shield its statewide voter
registration list from public disclosure.

We are urging the Supreme Court to take up a challenge to the Ninth
Circuit ruling and overturn the decision, citing federal law designed
to foster transparency that allows the use of voting rolls to uncover
fraud and errors. (Public Interest Legal Foundation petitioned the
Supreme Court for review in July 2026.)

This brief comes in the case _Public Interest Legal Foundation, Inc.
v. Scott T. Nago, in his official capacity as Hawaii’s Chief State
Election Officer_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38572&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuc3VwcmVtZWNvdXJ0Lmdvdi9zZWFyY2guYXNweD9maWxlbmFtZT0vZG9ja2V0L2RvY2tldGZpbGVzL2h0bWwvcHVibGljLzI2LTk4Lmh0bWwmdXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=e1ad01910e695d2394cfba21e300bbecaa6d608717bec35ddb08ec74fde50c1d]
(No. 26-98). We urge the court to grant Public Interest Legal
Foundation’s petition to have its case heard and resolve a conflict
among the federal appeals courts over whether statewide voter
registration lists must be made available under the National Voter
Registration Act (NVRA [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38573&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY29uZ3Jlc3MuZ292L2Nycy1wcm9kdWN0L1I0NTAzMD91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=eab5b97d5c60ead81c2432bcf26ec5b4f51a2c9a6a7aa2d9a9017e7dcf437fe3]).

In 2023, Public Interest Legal Foundation requested
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38574&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGVtb2NyYWN5ZG9ja2V0LmNvbS9jYXNlcy9oYXdhaWktdm90ZXItcm9sbC1hY2Nlc3MtY2hhbGxlbmdlLXBpbGYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=62e11653a2945f6c55a2a9f4769a3c4cc82017cade2950960bfd06d27ca67a12]
Hawaii’s statewide voter registration list under the NVRA’s public
disclosure provision. Hawaii refused. A federal district court
dismissed the case, and the Ninth Circuit affirmed. The Ninth Circuit
held that Hawaii’s statewide voter registration list is not a
“record concerning the implementation” of programs and activities
designed to ensure accurate and current voter lists under Section 8(i)
of the NVRA. The court instead directed
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38575&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly9jZG4uY2E5LnVzY291cnRzLmdvdi9kYXRhc3RvcmUvb3BpbmlvbnMvMjAyNi8wNC8yOC8yNC02NjI5LnBkZj91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=f0ed85d94199c775bc5919357965ac069a0ab5e03fd95d06257e97fb2ee71de6]
Public Interest Legal Foundation to obtain voter-registration
information from individual county clerks.

In our _amicus_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38571&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3B1YmxpYy1pbnRlcmVzdC1sZWdhbC12LW5hZ28taGF3YWlpLWVsZWN0aW9uLWFtaWN1cy05OC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=8df72eda1dde436b2698d382f27eb264aa9ce3df1af40230030a71b0afb192b3] brief
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38571&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3B1YmxpYy1pbnRlcmVzdC1sZWdhbC12LW5hZ28taGF3YWlpLWVsZWN0aW9uLWFtaWN1cy05OC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=8df72eda1dde436b2698d382f27eb264aa9ce3df1af40230030a71b0afb192b3],
we point out that federal law requires states to protect the integrity
of the electoral process by ensuring that accurate voter registration
rolls are maintained. The NVRA specifically provides the public access
to records concerning state voter-list maintenance activities.

We point out that its public records requests are critical in
evaluating NVRA compliance:

> As a result of its use of the state’s voter registration list and
> other election-related information and records published by the
> Election Assistance Commission, Judicial Watch’s efforts have led
> to the identification and removal of over six million outdated and
> ineligible names from voter rolls across nearly a dozen states.

We argue that Congress deliberately used broad language in requiring
disclosure:

> [The NVRA] requires states to “maintain” and “make
> available” to the public “all records concerning the
> implementation of programs and activities conducted for the purpose
> of ensuring the accuracy and currency of official lists of eligible
> voters.”

Our brief emphasizes that the plain language of Section 8(i)
encompasses the official statewide voter registration list:

> The plain meaning and ordinary terms of Section 8(i) clearly
> encompass the official list of eligible voters. It is the primary
> and ultimate end product that concerns the implementation of all
> state programs and activities to ensure an accurate voter
> registration list....

> The Ninth Circuit [held] that the voter registration list is not a
> record that concerns the implementations of programs and activities
> to ensure an accurate voter list. This ruling is not only wrong, but
> it also threatens electoral transparency nationwide and undermines
> the purposes for which Congress passed the NVRA.

> It also limits the ability of organizations such as Judicial Watch
> to enforce the list maintenance provisions of the NVRA. Judicial
> Watch often uses the statewide voter registration list to determine
> if jurisdictions are complying with the list maintenance
> requirements of the NVRA. The voter registration list is key to
> determining whether jurisdictions are properly inactivating and then
> cancelling registrants who have changed address. The voter
> registration list will show a voter’s status and whether a voter
> has been changed from active to inactive after receipt of a
> forwardable address confirmation notice. It can also find violations
> whenever a jurisdiction fails to cancel a registrant as required by
> the NVRA after notice and the passage of two general federal
> elections. The Ninth Circuit’s decision would allow states to
> withhold such critical records and to hide a failure to implement
> programs and activities necessary to ensure an accurate list.

We argue that the Ninth Circuit’s decision conflicts with the First
Circuit’s ruling that Maine’s statewide voter registration list is
subject to disclosure under the NVRA:

> [A] unanimous panel of the First Circuit had no problem finding that
> Maine’s statewide voter registration list was a record mandated to
> be disclosed by the NVRA. The Maine voter registration list
> “plainly relates to” the implementation of programs and
> activities for an accurate list since it “reflects the additions
> and changes made by Maine election officials ... as part of
> Maine’s voter list registration and maintenance activities.”

Our brief points out that our NVRA enforcement efforts focus
predominantly on the change-of-address procedure under Section 8(d):

> Oftentimes, jurisdictions will fail to timely mark a registrant
> inactive who received a confirmation notice, or will fail to remove
> the inactive registrant after the second general federal election of
> inactivity, leaving registrants who have long moved out of state on
> their rolls for years or sometimes decades. State voter registration
> lists then become filled with ineligible registrants and people
> registered in multiple states. As a result, “24 million voter
> registrations in the United States—about one in eight— are
> either invalid or significantly inaccurate.”

We are a national leader in election integrity and voting rights
litigation, with a record of successful lawsuits
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=37921&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdGFnL2VsZWN0aW9uLWxhdy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=70d598f89bd90d3885f269290a47b88637686b68832deee215bec6c500ffc6c2] enforcing
constitutional redistricting standards and cleaning voter rolls
nationwide.

Our lawsuits and legal actions have caused the removal of six million
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=37547&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaW5hY3RpdmUtdm90ZXJzLXJlbW92ZWQtY29sb3JhZG8tdm90ZXItcm9sbHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=7998d82757f5f93bb7c9c88992f1149d2e0d24d3f69c9713f37490381c48f097]
ineligible names from voter lists nationwide, including from Oregon
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=37696&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvb3JlZ29uLXZvdGVyLXJvbGxzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=f2d78b95899d42c293b95b0bf5901b579ba9a2727175b0f3c673c87819b97664], Colorado
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=37547&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaW5hY3RpdmUtdm90ZXJzLXJlbW92ZWQtY29sb3JhZG8tdm90ZXItcm9sbHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=7998d82757f5f93bb7c9c88992f1149d2e0d24d3f69c9713f37490381c48f097],
Kentucky

OBAMA’S ‘DIAPER DISPARITY’ PROGRAM GETS $29 MILLION

Apparently, America has a great diaper divide that can be eradicated
with millions of your tax dollars thrown at “diaper disparity.”
Our _Corruption Chronicles_ blog has the details
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=85047&L=38557&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZGlhcGVyLWRpc3Bhcml0eS1nZXRzLTI5LW1pbC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnMmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9Q01qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNE&hash=791c4e97d3e1e8abe0239d385ea45164b9eba0e17137d8b94512f063d161d98b].

clean_body: Obama’s ‘Diaper Disparity’ Program Gets $29 Million [INSIDE JW] JUDICIAL WATCH URGES SUPREME COURT TO PROTECT PUBLIC ACCESS TO STATE VOTER ROLLS [] We continue to insist that dirty voter rolls can mean dirty elections. We are again taking up the fight for clean elections by asking the Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) to make it clear that the public has a right to see states’ voter registration lists. We filed an amicus curiae [] (friend of the court) brief to the Supreme Court supporting the Public Interest Legal Foundation’s (PILF) petition for review of a Ninth Circuit decision that allows Hawaii to shield its statewide voter registration list from public disclosure. We are urging the Supreme Court to take up a challenge to the Ninth Circuit ruling and overturn the decision, citing federal law designed to foster transparency that allows the use of voting rolls to uncover fraud and errors. (Public Interest Legal Foundation petitioned the Supreme Court for review in July 2026.) This brief comes in the case Public Interest Legal Foundation, Inc. v. Scott T. Nago, in his official capacity as Hawaii’s Chief State Election Officer [] (No. 26-98). We urge the court to grant Public Interest Legal Foundation’s petition to have its case heard and resolve a conflict among the federal appeals courts over whether statewide voter registration lists must be made available under the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA []). In 2023, Public Interest Legal Foundation requested [] Hawaii’s statewide voter registration list under the NVRA’s public disclosure provision. Hawaii refused. A federal district court dismissed the case, and the Ninth Circuit affirmed. The Ninth Circuit held that Hawaii’s statewide voter registration list is not a “record concerning the implementation” of programs and activities designed to ensure accurate and current voter lists under Section 8(i) of the NVRA. The court instead directed [] Public Interest Legal Foundation to obtain voter-registration information from individual county clerks. In our amicus [] brief [], we point out that federal law requires states to protect the integrity of the electoral process by ensuring that accurate voter registration rolls are maintained. The NVRA specifically provides the public access to records concerning state voter-list maintenance activities. We point out that its public records requests are critical in evaluating NVRA compliance: As a result of its use of the state’s voter registration list and other election-related information and records published by the Election Assistance Commission, Judicial Watch’s efforts have led to the identification and removal of over six million outdated and ineligible names from voter rolls across nearly a dozen states. We argue that Congress deliberately used broad language in requiring disclosure: [The NVRA] requires states to “maintain” and “make available” to the public “all records concerning the implementation of programs and activities conducted for the purpose of ensuring the accuracy and currency of official lists of eligible voters.” Our brief emphasizes that the plain language of Section 8(i) encompasses the official statewide voter registration list: The plain meaning and ordinary terms of Section 8(i) clearly encompass the official list of eligible voters. It is the primary and ultimate end product that concerns the implementation of all state programs and activities to ensure an accurate voter registration list.... The Ninth Circuit [held] that the voter registration list is not a record that concerns the implementations of programs and activities to ensure an accurate voter list. This ruling is not only wrong, but it also threatens electoral transparency nationwide and undermines the purposes for which Congress passed the NVRA. It also limits the ability of organizations such as Judicial Watch to enforce the list maintenance provisions of the NVRA. Judicial Watch often uses the statewide voter registration list to determine if jurisdictions are complying with the list maintenance requirements of the NVRA. The voter registration list is key to determining whether jurisdictions are properly inactivating and then cancelling registrants who have changed address. The voter registration list will show a voter’s status and whether a voter has been changed from active to inactive after receipt of a forwardable address confirmation notice. It can also find violations whenever a jurisdiction fails to cancel a registrant as required by the NVRA after notice and the passage of two general federal elections. The Ninth Circuit’s decision would allow states to withhold such critical records and to hide a failure to implement programs and activities necessary to ensure an accurate list. We argue that the Ninth Circuit’s decision conflicts with the First Circuit’s ruling that Maine’s statewide voter registration list is subject to disclosure under the NVRA: [A] unanimous panel of the First Circuit had no problem finding that Maine’s statewide voter registration list was a record mandated to be disclosed by the NVRA. The Maine voter registration list “plainly relates to” the implementation of programs and activities for an accurate list since it “reflects the additions and changes made by Maine election officials ... as part of Maine’s voter list registration and maintenance activities.” Our brief points out that our NVRA enforcement efforts focus predominantly on the change-of-address procedure under Section 8(d): Oftentimes, jurisdictions will fail to timely mark a registrant inactive who received a confirmation notice, or will fail to remove the inactive registrant after the second general federal election of inactivity, leaving registrants who have long moved out of state on their rolls for years or sometimes decades. State voter registration lists then become filled with ineligible registrants and people registered in multiple states. As a result, “24 million voter registrations in the United States—about one in eight— are either invalid or significantly inaccurate.” We are a national leader in election integrity and voting rights litigation, with a record of successful lawsuits [] enforcing constitutional redistricting standards and cleaning voter rolls nationwide. Our lawsuits and legal actions have caused the removal of six million [] ineligible names from voter lists nationwide, including from Oregon [], Colorado [], Kentucky [] and New York City []. Judicial Watch legal pressure also resulted in voter roll clean-ups in Pennsylvania [], North Carolina [], and Ohio []. In July 2026, we announced [] that records from the Virginia Department of Elections showed the commonwealth cancelled 6,531 [] “declared noncitizen” voter registrations between June 2024 and June 2026. Also in July 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice announced its intention to file a motion to intervene [] in Judicial Watch’s federal lawsuit filed on behalf of a California political candidate and a state political party against the State of California due to its failure to maintain accurate voter rolls as required by the NVRA. A federal court in Illinois [] ruled that our lawsuit to force the cleaning of voter rolls may proceed in that state. In January 2026, in a historic case filed by Judicial Watch, the Supreme Court decided 7-2 [] in favor of Congressman Mike Bost and two presidential electors who were before the court to vindicate their standing to challenge an Illinois law allowing the counting of ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day. OBAMA’S ‘DIAPER DISPARITY’ PROGRAM GETS $29 MILLION Apparently, America has a great diaper divide that can be eradicated with millions of your tax dollars thrown at “diaper disparity.” Our Corruption Chronicles blog has the details []. A controversial initiative launched by former President Barack Obama—and handsomely funded under Biden—to end a fabricated pandemic of “diaper disparity” by providing needy families with government-subsidized diapers is quietly being kept alive by the Trump administration. It is known as Diaper Distribution Demonstration and Research Pilot (DDDRP) and it is funded by a Health and Human Services (HHS) division known as Administration for Children and Families (ACF) Office of Community Services (OCS). Under both Obama and Biden, the questionable program received a steady stream of taxpayer dollars, and the money continues flowing under Trump albeit with less fanfare and press releases in an apparent effort to avoid scrutiny. Congress has repeatedly denied laws to give needy families government-subsidized diapers—in addition to free medical care and food—yet Obama launched the diaper giveaway back in 2016 with a $10 million infusion. Congress had twice rejected legislation to give needy families free diapers and the White House at the time promoted the initiative as essential to eradicate a national “diaper divide” that would abolish “diaper disparity” by expanding access for America's poorest families. Obama’s White House Domestic Policy Director, Cecilia Muñoz, spearheaded the initiative, asserting diapers are imperative to babies’ health and “no family should have to choose between keeping their babies healthy and keeping the lights or heat on.” Months earlier Congress resoundingly rejected the second measure (Hygiene Assistance for Families of Infants and Toddlers Act) in four years to grant poor families government-subsidized diapers. Years earlier similar legislation (Diaper Investment and Aid to Promote Economic Recovery Act) also got slammed in Congress. Biden kept the program going with an $8 million gran [ [] in 2022 to provide diapers and diapering supplies through government distribution programs for families with low incomes. “One in three families in the U.S. with diaper-age children report having unmet diaper needs,” according to that grant document, issued by HHS. “Diaper need is largely defined as the lack of a sufficient supply of diapers to keep an infant/toddler clean, dry, and healthy,” the grant announcement further read, adding that “Infrequent diaper changes can lead to diaper rashes and urinary tract infections, compromising the health and well-being of infants and toddlers.” The lengthy document cited random studies on the impacts of diaper need, which of course, “disproportionately impacts families with low incomes and can have long-term, multigenerational effects,” according to the government. Besides the detrimental health effects on the infant, the studies referenced by HHS found associations between diaper need and parental stress, which can have negative, compounding effects on the health and well-being of both caregivers and children. As an example, the agency claimed childcare providers require an adequate supply of diapers, yet many low-income families cannot afford a consistent supply. “Therefore, diaper need can prevent infants and toddlers from being in early care settings and further exacerbate the impact of poverty by impeding caregivers’ ability to attend school, training programs, and/or work consistently,” according to the health agency. Another study used by HHS to make its case found that more than half of parents who rely on childcare have missed work because of an inadequate supply of diapers, which means “access to diapers represents both a public health concern for the well-being of children and a source of economic stress for parents and caretakers.” The great American diaper giveaway promised to lower anxiety and depression among parents, decrease rates of missed days for children in childcare, reduce family health issues by improving the health of caretakers and children, increase workforce participation and reduce economic stress by cutting unemployment. The new grant does not go into such detail but nevertheless commits $29 million [] to keep DDDRP going by “expanding ongoing diaper distribution programs” to meet the goal of delivering a regular, sufficient supply to caregivers and children with low incomes. “The American Public Health Association reports that one in three families in the United States with diaper-age children report having an unmet diaper need,” according to the government’s recently published grant announcement. “By providing families with a reliable supply of diapers and diapering essentials, the program supports the health, well-being, and healthy development of infants and toddlers.” Until next week, [Contribute] [] [32x32x1] [] [32x32x2] [] [32x32x3] [] [32x32x3] [] Judicial Watch, Inc. 425 3rd St Sw Ste 800 Washington, DC 20024 202.646.5172 © 2017 - 2026, All Rights Reserved Manage Email Subscriptions [] |

name: Democrats.org
subject: Would you take 50/50 odds?
body:
---
Derek, there are just 67 days left until Election Day, and _six_ critical Senate races are rated toss-ups by the Cook Political Report. Essentially, the races that will decide control of the Senate are a coin toss right now. **But in the most critical midterm election of our lifetimes, 50/50 odds just aren’t good enough.** [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-eom-august-2026?refcode=em_20260828_8829_fr&amount=7&refcode2=8829_22930333_yU1bbF&akid=8829%2E22930333%2EyU1bbF) Every single thing we do between now and November 3rd — every door we knock, every call we make, every voter we register, _every dollar we give to this people-powered movement_ — helps push the needle a little further in our direction. ### Peter —
This week we are focusing on the work being done in Minnesota. Eight legislative candidates stood together at the Minnesota State Capitol last Thursday and made a public commitment to govern across party lines after Election Day. Minnesota Forward Together, a coalition of DFL, Republican, Independent and Forward Independence legislative candidates, committed to working across party lines to solve problems for their constituents instead of trying to score political points They did not promise to agree on everything. They are promising to put their constituents ahead of their party and find common ground wherever they can. The Forward Party has been talking about the Fulcrum Strategy at the federal level all year. The argument is you don't need a majority of independent senators or representatives to change how Congress works. You need enough members who are independent from the control of either party to hold the balance of power on votes that matter. Minnesota Forward Together is that argument: built at the state level with eight candidates standing together who are running for office right now. **A note for readers outside Minnesota:** The DFL (The Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party) is Minnesota's Democratic Party. It was formed in 1944 through a merger of the Minnesota Democratic Party and the Farmer-Labor Party, which had been a powerful independent political force in the state since the 1920s. The DFL name reflects Minnesota's long tradition of coalition politics, the same tradition that Minnesota Forward Together is drawing on. It also reflects the work and growth of the MN Forward Party that formed through a merger last year. The Independence-Alliance Party of Minnesota and the Minnesota Forward Party merged to form the **Forward Independence Party of Minnesota. The merged organization is bringing candidates together that share our values and ultimately driving more choices in front of the voters.** So when you see DFL candidates committing to govern alongside Republicans and independents, it is worth knowing that the party itself was founded on the principle that different political movements could come together around shared values. Politicians from different parties sharing a stage and making this pledge reflects the current stage of our democracy. It reflects that this kind of promise has grown uncommon among our representatives. Putting the needs of constituents first should be expected of our state and federal leaders. What makes Minnesota Forward Together significant is the timing. These candidates are making a public pledge before they are elected. They are choosing accountability now and presenting their intentions to voters before they are safely in office. They are publicly announcing to the people of Minnesota that they are better served by legislators who talk to each other than by legislators who perform for their base. **The Bigger Picture** **Minnesota Is the State-Level Version of What We're Building Nationally.** The Fulcrum Strategy in the U.S. Senate says a small bloc of genuinely independent senators, two to three members who answer only to their states and not to either party, can hold the balance of power in a closely divided chamber. Neither party can pass anything without them. That changes the incentive structure for everyone. Legislation has to earn their vote on the merits, not on party loyalty. Minnesota Forward Together is enacting a model of that strategy with a cross-partisan coalition of state legislators who have committed publicly to governing together. Pledging to agree where they can, and disagree where they must, is a vehicle for changing how a state legislature operates. In an evenly divided state house like Minnesota currently has, this coalition would be incredibly powerful in advocating for principled reforms. **_The principle is identical._** You don't need a majority. You need a committed coalition that refuses to be owned by either side. Minnesota Forward Together is what that looks like when eight people decide to do it before they even win. **Imagine what it looks like when they do.**

### Friends,
It has been an incredibly difficult time throughout our state, as extreme weather and hardship hit several parts of the state, including Northwest Indiana and just north of our district in Ravenswood and Rocky Ripple.

The devastation so many of our neighbors experienced is truly heartbreaking, and I am continuing to hold close all those who were impacted throughout Indiana.

During this time, I have also seen people from every corner of District 46 showing up for those who need it.

I have seen you all sharing information on how to help Gary, filling sandbags in Rocky Ripple and trudging through floodwater in Ravenswood; you have consistently shown up for those who need it.

That is one of the many things that makes this community special.

Being the heart of the city means that we are used to hosting. That Hoosier hospitality we are always talking about is truly a way of life for the people who call District 46 home.

The past couple of weeks, you have shown that also means taking care of each other. Not just the people visiting for the week, but every person who calls this state home every day of the year.

While our neighbors across the state continue the long road towards full recovery, I know that District 46 will keep showing up where we are needed, and support our fellow Hoosiers in restoring their communities.

Thank you for being a partner in this work and thank you for looking out for one another.

It is such an honor to serve alongside you.
---
* * *
---
# **Federal Aid for Extreme Weather**
---
| [](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AA0AAAAAAQkOIJWzSn00rUolZzc4fw0vLANZIWGTRPdOfNFMekpxT88_wCZrFEPMP7zoBPmu4nX-E6PO9wk4Phn6Z7pADfNoZDyxajMhe2Y)
---
For families who have spent the past several weeks clearing debris, replacing what was lost and trying to understand how they will rebuild, this assistance matters. FEMA has approved Individual Assistance for Hoosiers affected by the severe storms and flooding in 21 Indiana counties, **including Marion County.** Eligible residents may receive help with temporary housing, essential home repairs, personal property losses and other disaster-related expenses not fully covered by insurance. Federal assistance cannot erase the hardship families have endured, but it can provide meaningful support during a long and difficult recovery. If you were affected, please do not assume you are ineligible or try to navigate this process alone. Apply by Oct. 25 at [DisasterAssistance.gov](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AA0AAAAAAQkOIJW0Xx6K08xHId3ma8V5cW1TDKcSpKl165_MFwAWxvAD59mHgCz55-IDYhI5w2Gam3g3xYRLQQA7yaoCG-g1sR3t78Bwtms "https://www.disasterassistance.gov/") or call 1-800-621-3362 for help with your application. Please share this information with anyone who may need it. Recovery begins with making sure every family knows what help is available and how to access it.
* * *
---
| | | |
---
| |
---
In addition to the federal benefits, there are also many state resources available to those impacted by the extreme weather that has been seen across our state. Households that receive SNAP benefits and lost food due to storm damage or power outages may be eligible for replacement benefits. Affected individuals must submit an affidavit for replacement benefits. **The affidavit must be submitted by Aug. 31, and the loss (due to power outage, flood, etc.) must be verified. **The document may be uploaded to the [FSSA Benefits Portal](https://click.subscription.in.gov/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5ODN9AA0AAAAAAQkOIJW1tq6mjdDC9r_GduDYC6XviWscLCRZbOdSKeJE3W8V9awpob6Jo6ltog1vO5zIQ5HwzA_Fy6CiS1IGoaPJPx8DMu-DgqM), faxed to 888-436-9199 or dropped off at any Division of Family Resources' office.
* * *
---
|
---
**Your Voice Belongs in Indiana's Budget**
Indiana will soon make decisions about billions of public dollars. Those decisions will reach into your home, your school, your hospital and your community. They will determine whether you can afford childcare, whether an aging parent can receive care at home, whether your school can keep teachers in the classroom and whether your community has the resources to recover when crisis comes. **Decisions that consequential should not begin in a Statehouse conference room. They should begin with you.** That is why Indiana Senate Democrats are launching an eight-community Listening Tour before the 2027 budget session. We are leaving the Statehouse and coming to communities across Indiana to hear what life actually looks like for you right now. I want to hear what your family is carrying. What costs have become impossible to ignore? What help is hardest to find? What opportunities are slipping further out of reach? And if you could put one priority at the center of Indiana's next budget, what would it be? **We are not asking you to fit your life into the priorities government has already chosen. We are asking you to help shape those priorities from the beginning.** Our first stop is Indianapolis, and I hope you will join us. This will not be a presentation or a carefully scripted conversation. We are coming to listen openly, take your experiences seriously and carry what we hear into the 2027 legislative session. Because a state budget is more than a collection of numbers. It is a statement of who matters, what we value and what kind of future we are willing to build together. **You are Indiana. Your life should be visible in the choices your state makes, and your voice should be present wherever your money is spent.**
### _Join Us in Indianapolis_
**Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026**
**6 -8 p.m.**
**P30 at The Post Banquet Hall**
**3039 Post Road
Indianapolis, IN** The event is free and open to everyone. **Come with your questions, your concerns and your hopes for this state. We are ready to hear you.**
### We Are Coming Across Indiana
* **Sept. 12:** New Albany
* **Sept. 18:** Fishers
* **Sept. 19:** Zionsville
* **Sept. 26:** Highland
* **Oct. 3:** Elkhart
* **Oct. 10:** Fort Wayne
* **Oct. 17:** Portage

Additional details will be announced soon. Find the stop closest to you, bring a neighbor and help us build a state budget that reflects the people it is meant to serve. **YOUR life. YOUR priorities. YOUR voice. Indiana 's budget should reflect all three.**

body:
This is Trump’s ace in the hole to rig the upcoming midterm elections.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001xWQAt8zJEoh1jwUss-A7H3hUzGPKWGTp4xXvooHhjbQLW3G_36pmo585KDezZ9aXnDkcQSMqbblSD9gzmOd3abmOLs24_e4BfBSKjSDjkYHoItRcRA46muJZ3ogf3M6UrH8RP1L_5U0W9lDrbGefXvezk_2KXsWUxqoYiqToTpOqkOiPYadMjuQ7xstIYqVvFc6IY-QIQcIoiJ4CDUtajs_N2KlKO0ibCJAVB36sIexqXY0vtfzNfA==&c=umueIiWwTAuPLum8OgwSLMCf7tqBhz0kpR_0ZQOTV5MlaFe5jtkhMw==&ch=ytHeJmyMbHCILeFbLTJdK9SojyFF2tY8qoVEw82XmQZ_GQ3rtRGL7Q==)
---
|
Peter,
The US Postal Service finalized their plot to effectively ban mail-in ballots ahead of the November midterm elections. The new finalized rule enacts Trump's March executive order, an order federal courts have repeatedly blocked.
Under the rule, states must share voter data with the USPS. The USPS then "examines" that data to decide if a voter is eligible for a ballot. If a state refuses to share that sensitive voter data, the USPS won't deliver ballots in that state.
This rule would give the Trump admin control over who receives ballots and who doesn't.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001xWQAt8zJEoh1jwUss-A7H3hUzGPKWGTp4xXvooHhjbQLW3G_36pmo585KDezZ9aXnDkcQSMqbblSD9gzmOd3abmOLs24_e4BfBSKjSDjkYHoItRcRA46muJZ3ogf3M6UrH8RP1L_5U0W9lDrbGefXvezk_2KXsWUxqoYiqToTpOqkOiPYadMjuQ7xstIYqVvFc6IY-QIQcIoiJ4CDUtajs_N2KlKO0ib_c1remF_4fCwgUDwS2Lnww==&c=umueIiWwTAuPLum8OgwSLMCf7tqBhz0kpR_0ZQOTV5MlaFe5jtkhMw==&ch=ytHeJmyMbHCILeFbLTJdK9SojyFF2tY8qoVEw82XmQZ_GQ3rtRGL7Q==)
---
We do not have to imagine how Trump uses this power. Live in a heavily Democratic area? No ballot. Have a name that sounds Black or Hispanic? No ballot. They are not hiding what this is.
This is Trump's ace in the hole to rig the upcoming midterm elections. If you have been following our work, you know the Constitution gives states, not the federal government, the responsibility for administering elections. But the Trump admin is betting that the MAGA-occupied Supreme Court will let this rule stand anyway.
And that's where it gets scary. We have seen how partisan SCOTUS has become. They overturned Roe. They gutted the Voting Rights Act. They handed Trump criminal immunity. This court has been fully exposed as a puppet of Trump and MAGA extremists.

Sean Duffy, Michael Alfonso, and State Assemblyman Calvin Callahan joined Lincoln County Republicans at Rock Island Bar in Merrill. Michael Alfonso also did butter carving at the Lincoln County Fair and stopped by the Lincoln County GOP booth. **Buffalo County**
Buffalo County hosted a picnic to meet the candidates on August 23rd at beautiful Tourist Park in Mondovi. With a nice group attending and some great food, we hosted David Varnam, Eric Toney by phone, Rep. Treig Pronschinske, Joe Mueller standing in for Jay Schroeder, and Scott Bolstad for Sen. Ron Johnson. Ginny Gunderson was also there and represented the Mondovi City Council. The weather was perfect, and the information received was very helpful. **Monroe County**
Monroe County GOP held its first Movie Night on Thursday, August 13th, featuring Truth and Treason. They also participated in three parades in Norwalk, Bangor, and Leon, and celebrated 3 Back the Blue Mondays. **Vilas County**
On August 22nd, the Vilas County Republicans "opened shop" for two hours to display and hand out candidate yard signs in the parking lot of a friendly conservative in Eagle River, WI. They also had banners, T-shirts, and cold drink cozies. They handed out signs to enthusiastic conservatives who drove by that Saturday, from those who live in the Northwoods to a few from outside Vilas County. **Fond du Lac County**
Last Wednesday, August 19, the Fond du Lac Co. Republican Party held a Lincoln Day Dinner. **St. Croix County**
Hundreds gathered at River Bend to hear from Riley Gaines, Rachel Campos Duffy, Michael Alfonso, and Scarlett Johnson at a special rally organized with Turning Point Action and Moms for Liberty, where Chairman Rust presented Riley Gaines with a St. Croix County Chairman's Coin for her outstanding work fighting for women's rights. Republicans then showed up at the Hammond Heartland Days Parade with State Rep. Rob Kreibich, the North Hudson Pepper Fest Parade, where Tom Tiffany and Eric Toney handed out more than 75 Tiffany yard signs, and Save WI Saturday, which recruited six new Team Tiffany applicants with those same special guests. Volunteers also celebrated at a Primary Election Night Watch Party with Clerk of Court primary winner Kathy Kittel, wrote over 400 postcards for Tom Tiffany over ice cream at the Victory Center, and gathered for the August Executive Board Meeting. **Door County**
Door County Republicans had a great time at their fair booth earlier this month! **Waukesha County**
On Wednesday, August 12th, Waukesha County Republicans gathered for their monthly Movie Night; they showed "Young Washington" to a very enthusiastic crowd. On Saturday and Sunday, August 15th and 16th, they had a table at Mukwonago Maxwell St. Days, distributing Tiffany yard signs. **Green County**
The Republican Party of Green County held its monthly breakfast meeting on Saturday, August 8th with guest speakers Bob Spindell from the Wisconsin Elections Commission and Jon Aleckson for the 50th Assembly District. **Washington County**
Washington County Republicans have been keeping busy hosting a campaign bootcamp, participating in the Richfield parade, joining Tom Tiffany for a Tavern Talk, and knocking on doors! ## US Clears Sea Mines from Hormuz
The U.S. military has [cleared the Iranian sea mines](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAUhJ8Gd6zsg_8oKDaK6G6kKJFSWhgfLyfBYAFeZ_P0kfcVbjszGs18vz6mD0OewuOb2VCVNU4Bz-yxFEzTka1HkzIlEzYKmF_xSJ5WnKCGntcjBzkZW-iJU2uqRa2IgKJC1QzjIOUgR6icstB0XTeKZlwsjP1oLHSzkMKuOC-ttRWpq68eQTZ13TfyNg9dW0s5iF5ib0XP2hoXKjHdfkcKxeHqX_GJ6WbjVnnlStkzE3cGmoE-z_O25XB5DDQGfmQG-rrFQMfiMDHQxZnC82H_YOKUedzfOf4wFDIvDvmx75i4M2HhFN7KbErxyNeYuItpO_4x0Cbx-x3m_u_3n0zoaGlh4uuXCyee-QemvUpq2U_ynnI_sLZ-bIb8e3b5JO2ngv8BAAD__wIxlnI) from the Strait of Hormuz's international shipping lanes in what CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper called "a major milestone" in the six-month-old war with Iran. _"That sucker is open,"_ President Trump said in an interview. Navy divers, Navy SEALs, and air power from all four military branches [carried out the operation](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkT2O4zAMhU8jdwwU2WNZhYpt3M22WxochYo5qx9DkhNkT79QrjAdAT4-4Pv453P7RA6c7r8xkm0-b4meNVBrVLazukBYKhdMkRPVVz5LYE-bkmoGuYAyG7rGD9omHG7WEykaB7JXvWhjtFnUsFupzO1D03WWRk7kJ42LHBc3LV8GtXc0sO19clHmKuV8NZcv_TFJY_Q4G5rdOItJ0o1bLpfvzKnt5MMrP6hcXI5DsHtrRxXjL6FWodb0OnJtfSXU2ouFWuXSZy3UelbohEKtjlJzOQKmlM_kqEJtBblB9rDnEs9_UHc-Dk53CJioAhYCX4h6ojthTFAJ4e0GIpa_PRvxOxeIHKi2nAg4QdvpfQBPLEKtQ7G348khcJ21mOQ9Ioc3S_vhCx5W_Q8AAP__0jud8Q) under dangerous conditions.

U.S. forces have escorted nearly 1,500 commercial vessels carrying close to 750 million barrels of crude oil through the strait. Meanwhile, Iran's crude oil exports have plunged to about 260,000 barrels per day, [down more than 80%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAUhE8DmZExrH8CB5uQ9aYbood5bt6MsZHthunbj5grTFIqqaSvVPX_MT-AAsXnP9jRVp_miFcJWCvm-VVcQMiFMsSdIpZ3euVAHmfBhWRcM2FmcJVOnEdoV-sRBQ4t2l5pZYwyWrSbleuyolR-8AP02MMADrTrteJuHL3iLdmbx7UwPeeyN92i_ozcGDVIg9INshk5rlRT7j4SxbqhD-90Yu5c2ttgt1qP0gx_GzE1Yrquq3NxcXfYiOlGN2Li-va3RDjfbAnJfcKK7N7GEgWGX0fKtbAC0VVKsbCaX_vRbXUPbbbrcVEIVKRqRv7cgcJPef3lZ6cV3wEAAP__EDaBqQ) from a year ago.
## Trump Targets Changes in Beef Processing
President Trump announced Friday that he would seek regulatory changes to let [farmers and ranchers process their own food](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAQhZ8Gd0QE2xgKim3c3W23tCYwxLPiJ4JJrvL2q-wr3O5IRzo63_fn6_gCylTvv6Gg59SOit8jIzP24zlCRuiDOtRCFce7PXumhIdW2khlpXYHBKYXHgtM0SdEjfOE_rrZzbnNWT2dPqJb1vmGELbFmmjsGtCaoA06a0yCifxnT1ntrkqZq7vctnVRzm2zcWjCbMSiMBK3fvnbqPKJKb_bC_sltDJlfzI_hph_Cb0LvfOJJ-X86YTez1bwgyT0DrFQpcEdmFoVejdqNXZ1MrYKOUruz_KQCXrBPmSHGs5PSK1F-egt4BhU7_KGmCRDp5TkDZgzCr1P3cfHN-VMw2xiUfcC9P_CxD-0-vL6XwAAAP__NTGPXw), calling the four major meatpackers a "nasty Monopoly" that makes life "miserable" for producers. The announcement followed Trump's decision last week to allow 300,000 metric tons of tariff-free beef imports into the U.S. to help battle high prices. That move drew sharp criticism from American ranchers and sent cattle futures tumbling. On Friday, Trump [posted on Truth Social](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6yAUxvGngS0RHDCYgeFKV97SqVJHC-Pj-FTYWIAT5e2r9BW6fp_0G_5ft_EWKNF-_wgb-rbkccdnTdgalvGsMWEolUrYN9qxvvJZEi04ggBzEf0F3BhioweOOvDZL4iAiqOXtrfOWdcDX72CKThr47SIuIQumjl0qDX0vbVzVBMn__ZED04KYaS7TrbTwjmrjEMTlWFa4Ewtl-t3pr2tuKRXfmC5xrzx5NfWjsrUPwYDg6GVs601Rwrp_b9HLQqG9D_vIc2f5dwOBsORa6sMBimttEoKp8Eo1UkrePHz8aSUqBrLtLhvgX4p3v5Y6OHhJwAA___ujnmC) that he was "authorizing legal documents to be drawn in order to allow Farmers and Ranchers to be given the right to PROCESS THEIR OWN FOOD." Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins promised to begin [rolling back regulations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQAF8DmZFpGMCBg0vI5tILkcFtpm8NRt0GNL9fzX5h81KVVP-e09NRpH396za0OaRpx1si5ow8nbJEdCzEbt9oR3mnkyMFnEBDp_SgwExuyXTh1LrS24AI2JRo637ojenNAOXLoh-6pfb-AY1pjcHZwRx07cG7Ftq5Kcl-fHoAU2vd1aaa-0erjembzmC3NF3RavSUE1f_E-35hSG-04VcLWkro33lfEjR_ClgLGC877sKjreD08oo8oEKGCNdKDktXwWMmc_tUCEml0VFFFGM6xldprSrkFjNiEEdnBYUSSwlW3_cFCNJ1xetXjdH8Seef_nssvAdAAD___4WhPg) Monday. It remains unclear whether the change requires congressional action.

It is time for the Democrats.
We already did the list of people I think could run for president on the Republican side, and I put them into a tier list. Now we are going to do the same thing for the Democrats.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/736bd804-fe34-4488-a6a3-584daf614d1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The criteria are the same:
* Can they win a primary?
* Can they win a general election?
* Can they raise the money and build the infrastructure needed for a national campaign?
* And do they have the charisma and personality to go out there and actually woo people?

We have not even made it to the 2026 midterms. We do not know who is going to control the House or the Senate. But right after those midterms, people are going to start coming out of the woodwork and saying they are running for president.
So why speculate this early?
**Because it is fun!**
The Republican field could shrink quickly if Donald Trump immediately endorses JD Vance or somebody else. A lot of Republicans probably would not go against the grain. If Trump holds his endorsement until later in the primaries, though, that field could remain huge.
Democrats do not have a succession plan because they are not the party in power. That means everybody with a little money, a little name recognition, and a little ambition is going to look in the mirror and see a future POTUS.
I could see more than 20 people entering this thing. I have 31 names on my list, so let's get into it.
* * *
## The Unicorn Tier
### Michelle Obama
She is not running.
Michelle Obama has repeatedly said she does not want to run for president, but everybody always says the same thing: _**" If Michelle ran..."**_
If she did run, she would be an S-tier candidate. She would rally the troops, raise a ridiculous amount of money, immediately have national political clout, and go very, very far in the primary.
Personally, I think she would win the primary and the general election. She could be the next president of the United States.
But she is not doing it.
That is why Michelle Obama belongs in the unicorn tier.
* * *
## D Tier
### Kirsten Gillibrand, Xavier Becerra, Tom Steyer, Sheryl Sandberg
All of these people have different problems. Some are accomplished politicians. Some come from the business world. All of them would have to make a serious case for why Democratic voters should care about their candidacies.
Most of them are not particularly well known nationally.
Tom Steyer is the exception. He ran for president in 2020 and then spent an enormous amount of his own money running for governor of California in 2026. He received about 23 percent of the primary vote but [failed to advance to the general election](https://substack.com/redirect/51b95f17-9b1f-40bb-bc2c-593427900c6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Does he decide that this is finally his time to be POTUS? Maybe. He certainly has the money. I could also see him deciding that he is done running for office.
If Steyer entered the presidential race using the same economic and affordability messaging he used in California, he could start in D tier and slowly work his way up until he was one of the last people standing on a debate stage.
Everybody else has a massive hill to climb when it comes to fundraising and name recognition.
* * *
## C Tier
### Ritchie Torres, Abigail Spanberger, Jasmine Crockett, Mark Cuban, Amy Klobuchar
These people are better known, but their politics, personal baggage, and position inside the Democratic Party put them at a disadvantage.
Most of them would struggle to raise enough money to remain competitive, with the possible exceptions of Mark Cuban. Cuban is rich.
Cuban has already said that he is [not running for president in 2028](https://substack.com/redirect/54ce8f4e-497f-4793-ac5a-b05bdb87aca2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He has also suggested that, if he ever did run, he might do it as a Republican because he does not believe he could win a Democratic primary.
Maybe I should have put him on the Republican list. Then again, I do not really think he is running as a Republican, either.
Everyone in this tier has work to do in almost every category.
Jasmine Crockett's charisma and social media presence could propel her into the later stages of a primary.
Everybody else? Eh.
I think Democratic voters are probably tired of Amy Klobuchar and some of the other familiar names.
* * *
## B Tier
### Chris Murphy, Ro Khanna, Ruben Gallego, Cory Booker, Elissa Slotkin, Rahm Emanuel, and Tim Walz
These are all people with political clout and at least some fundraising ability. Some have more personality than others, but almost everyone in this group could be compelling on a debate stage.
Ro Khanna is one of the B-tier candidates I could see remaining in the race through the later primaries. I could also see Chris Murphy sticking around.
I do not personally like [Ro Khanna's Substack](https://open.substack.com/pub/rokhannausa?utm_source=mentions) as a presidential candidate, and in general, but I can see how he could shape his campaign to win over Democratic primary voters. The problem is that I am not convinced he could win a general election.
That is the dichotomy inside the Democratic Party. What appeals to the progressive base during a primary does not always square with what swing voters and independents want in November.
People like Tim Walz, Elissa Slotkin, and Cory Booker could fall off quickly.
Rahm Emanuel is a Democrat from a different time. He has plenty of name recognition, and he is already making the rounds, but this is not his Democratic Party anymore.

## Ross Fire Second-Largest in North Texas
The Ross Fire in Palo Pinto and Jack counties has burned more than [85,000 acres](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuSnTAMhp8GOp8x5mYXFGnoNm1KxtgCKzEWY4vDJk-fYV9hS-mf-f7Lr4_lw2LEtP-0B0z8udGS4C4RmCEvHOAfrNmWDHzl5ChG2GEjWpRUg5BaKLNYx_iGpbO1n1bpTVPD1IxaS9m0_VCHSXdKur7d-l5rqVs3mnbwjdFd51bbD77G6cFJrUzTSNW2L-NBy3YbrdpWY7SqOgkemfKLAzB82rLFv_SG_HJ01HEKzGep2h-Vmis13_f9Sqvz2_3IlZqfRpWaIzkbn5MyB_GFETdGv2EGcVwlZKLjeXHAJAJduYiM54lpFxwyXXsQ2SYXok2-CEzitJHEiYlJ_Lbuj3B0JUZ4zDo5jENvKjXXefLnjTFiGcaqk_thMX4F5-8O_p7U_wAAAP__BGOZHA) and was 26% contained Friday morning, per the Texas A&M Forest Service. The blaze started Monday, almost 100 miles west of Dallas. Hundreds of firefighters and volunteers are battling what is now the [second-largest wildfire](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ9GOwz-sgoFxTV2e-2VBuFHSVjZwH-yd09_cV_huklmMl9mvu7L3YQYju3TPFDTy6flwFoiEmFeaMdfXLMpGek7HzbFiBv6lBbgMDIuGajFWAonLsK0Tq_cqb5F3U9Sct4Pt7Hd9c1PXggrzGRug4MRcXVcTlL1SlllXRv0VcclqL7nMAydcij54CcDflVKQiM4ukApd7Qj4csUH3_Sibmz6dFGvRM9SzN8NDA3MNdaO59e4hpyBRqYL9nAnFMpzIeMLBR2pMoK2nQ4Fk3esBCrIbq3jSdmdqRMO3vj2qzds4YYQxmnRvDtYUJ8w-m_p50a_gIAAP__pgmFFg) in North Texas history, roughly five times the size of DFW International Airport. The cause remains under investigation, and officials have set no containment timeline. Crews are trying to hold the fire east of Highway 16, near Possum Kingdom Lake, where a 2011 wildfire destroyed 166 homes. Five structures were lost, and a 97-year-old Scout camp reported [catastrophic damage](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZB61mz87cHAJ2Vx6ITLQBp8MHtk9w-w-_Yp5hU1KFZS-UtW_-3h3IYZj_et2svz2aTzoLJGYKY-80TdN2ZVM_MzHnGKklXxKIwJ2ErREM7qZw4vGxlWLnWAxqiKreq0BVN121Wb9hF5R07XOLxOYbkYw1KvGt0DNPEMV7IUDjUYpwLq-mYU01L536CdjNIoGaAmc8o03Ynq74uNXelG-zWmvot2YH0XUfwQOAodrgPyfnvlw8QoIHC6-wAH05S_5QGROpUgfMkkFIPcQqciTCsvk5eJidEWuOZ1FcpK6BQDp5kxF4FBluzzOEGMoXS8aWHcXPmUV__bFl8WfAAAA__8A-oZN). "_We are still in the midst of putting this fire out,"_ spokeswoman Amy Meyer said.
## Trump Honors Artemis II Crew in Houston
President Trump awarded the [Congressional Space Medal](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GOtBic4dduEhD96dNiRZ7OVYyNrL3P-7y9NGlyAuknZFG832_vpYv5Mjp8RMPcvLa8pLoqpFEqCyy029aC9ZC8l2SzzHSg7acFwXq3oHplF3QCz9pGbENboVgh5bcMBkDMOjbvd2dH1cY1Ga9RmOUn8YbmdF7qzXAAGFq2X3mwCg7DKC07m0gA3qbUG2rtUY1I1BgyaWXnYReWLf4zk8qvc9HG90uctZG_2jU3Kj5uq4-rf7D8ekbNZ85srCvjZqlfB9nh-HgxFUKCuf0L64neurQY6Dj3SWs2B0cWbC8u-IT3uxoJmiLC-fFMXK9T80IjwM5_n0i_2vw6dSfAAAA__-4R4id) of Honor to the four Artemis II astronauts on Friday at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, then became the first president to call astronauts aboard the International Space Station from Mission Control. NASA's Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen completed a 10-day [mission around the moon](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2P3CAQQH8N7ljB-AsKijTuLm1KawzjNREGC8Z7l_z6aPMXrn7S09P79bF-YEwxP3_iSY6_9rJm-myJmKmufNBf2iq2SnzX7EtK9KS9lBUUTFIZCXZFz_FF64BdcJsKVnfk9GyMUrofp-5wY5g82HnwGnDDcQ9aBUS_WaPsbPqpi-6tUwas1gr6_mEDGdXvM8K-WWtADIpC5FIffBDTF7Y9_Skvqg9fzi65g_lqov8hYBGw4ObnNxCwXKWxgIXrfV7yKLlUiZXpjE3GKLFxLRlvbjJjwyZ_lyO3kmW70JP0lJmqPMrduGQBi7bzMI4TCFi66sL1GVOKbZrFoJ4nxvS_hr978eXgXwAAAP__y7WJOQ) in April, the first crewed lunar voyage in more than 50 years. During the ceremony, Trump signed an [executive order](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQhZ8Gd7ZgwH8FRRp3N21KC8OwIGFjwex6k6ePvMkb3G6k-fTpnPPra_0yMcXj8dPsqOnt83rgVRMSYVkp4B_ciqkF6VkOm1PCB_qcV-AwtHxqYV6NpfjCVZnG6Y27WTSoxThNnAvZD03Qw-jQCvBjbz1OqrfezUI4OW4bl0KpJupbxyeYheAgZTc7nLj0owG_zfMETHF0kXLpKCDh21SffucXls7mvUk6EJ2VyR8MFgbLdV1dyM9K-bCh5CPahDfIYLm7MVj-f9uPisFST2ORwWIK3fC_C_dYW1Op5MM8qbY7OpPakI9cWgDFR9XL7gxnU7Q7r5hSrMPIFH_sJqZPMPruoC8NfwMAAP__V2qN8A) creating a U.S. Space Academy, a new military academy that will also train civilians for NASA and commercial spaceflight. He said the nation must "educate and train an entire generation" of service members and engineers. The academy's location has yet to be determined.
## Zebras Trot Back into Fort Worth Zoo
The Fort Worth Zoo [announced Friday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O4yAUBeCnwZ0tfLGNKSi2ocu2W1r8XGIkYiJ8N2Ty9KNMHmHqI52j7_y7bBebcjquf-0NNT1j2Q5sZ0YirBvt-EJX7VmR_tfDl5zxirGUDTgsPV97UJv1lB64TbYL2vGgxg71KNeV81HMS7frBYWUfpZOoeLTPEY5KufVOrsA1svQJf2u4yuoceQgxKACrlxEaSE6pVZgE8eQqNSBdiR82jPmr_LAOvhy67Leie4nE38YGAamtTYczofY3jED8xYxMLl4mxmYD6n_mHoqfSyV-lYq7f2rFAZm4osSi2BguqrDvaWc07lINvHrzab8s0q_feuh4TsAAP__tf9_pA) that two juvenile zebras from a private Texas wildlife ranch are now exploring their habitat, becoming the zoo's first since 2021. Hercules and Pegasus, half-brothers whose names film fans will recognize from Disney's 1997 _Hercules_ , arrived about a month ago. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Does it help the American people? Yes or No?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
I wish I were kidding

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3005%2E4032634%2EsaKnX9)
---
I think I've finally figured out how Donald Trump makes decisions. You know, when you look at the things he supports — and the things he ignores — there's a pretty simple pattern. It's basically a decision tree: | [](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3778?t=8&akid=3005%2E4032634%2EsaKnX9)
---
Healthcare? He doesn't care. Housing crisis? Big yawn. Wages for working families? Not Trump’s concern.
If it doesn't help him personally, if it doesn't line billionaires' pockets, then the answer is always the same: Trump just doesn't care.
I wish this were an exaggeration, but we know it is true from his record:
He rushed through crypto giveaways while stalling on housing.
He's handed out pardons to people who'd do him favors while blocking policies that would help families afford insulin.
He's carved out tax loopholes for the wealthy while letting working people fall further behind.
He's started unnecessary forever wars while the price of oil skyrockets.
He's used millions to tear apart the White House to create gold-lined ballrooms while you wonder how you'll afford groceries.
When something helps Donald Trump, his family, his billionaire friends, or the biggest corporations in America, he moves fast. No delays. No excuses. Just action.
When something would actually make life better for ordinary American families, suddenly there's always an excuse, a delay, or nothing at all.
That's the Trump decision-making process. And once you understand it, a whole lot of his presidency starts to make sense.
**I'm going to keep calling Donald Trump out — every corrupt deal, every self-serving bad decision, every time he puts himself and his billionaire friends ahead of the American people. And I'm not letting up until there are enough people in Washington willing to stand up to him.**
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

"The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text.

The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education.

Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation.

You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph.

This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs.

clean_body: Convicted because of a cooler | | | | | | Dear Fellow American,This officer was just convicted of manslaughter for trying to stop a fleeing criminal with non-lethal force. Sgt. Erik Duran dedicated 15 years of his life to the NYPD.He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. Now he's fighting for his own freedom – All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx. | | | | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him. The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: News, Not Narrative – Why We Built the Wire
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/thewire?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
**Newspapers have long been the lifeblood of American democracy.** They mattered before there was an America. Franklin was a printer. Hamilton, Madison, and Jay made their case for the Constitution in New York newspapers.

As America grew from thirteen states on the eastern seaboard into a continental nation of fifty, newspapers grew with it. By the middle of the last century, thousands of papers covered states, towns, and even small counties.

Their critical role is to let people at the state and local level see who exercised power in their name, and what they did with it. **It is hard to imagine America becoming the democracy it did without them.**

Yet that is precisely what we now face. Imagine America without local or state newspapers.

You do not need to imagine it. Since 2005, more than 3,000 local newspapers have closed—around 40 percent of them. Here in Mississippi, Buckley Newspapers shut the Jasper County News and the Smith County Reformer in June 2024. The Reformer had published since 1889.

Advertising dollars moved to the big social media platforms. Local newspapers can no longer pay reporters to cover their own communities.

More of the content is generic. Less of it is truly local news.

Hollowed out, newspapers increasingly cover what local television is reporting, while television reports what local newspapers and radio already treat as relevant. **The media landscape becomes an echo chamber.** Into that echo chamber pours social media, where a provocative claim travels faster than a reported fact—and from there into conventional wisdom, and finally into public policy.

**One consequence of having so few reporters cover so much is that what is presented as news is often just a press release.** A public body meets, makes a series of interesting decisions, and reveals a great deal—and the press release says only what somebody wanted said about it.

Without a local reporter sitting there, taking notes, how does the public really find out what public officials are up to? Budgets are set to spend your money without the public knowing what was spent, or on what. School boards vote on your children’s schooling with no parent in the room.

One attempt to address this has been to set up nonprofit media organizations. Mississippi has its fair share of them. They are often well meaning, and the state is better off for them. But they tend to focus on what is happening statewide, not locally. Nonprofit outlets seldom sit through the Yazoo City council or the Madison County school board.

Worse, the nonprofit model can turn news into propaganda. Some of those pumping money into the Mississippi media landscape are doing so in order to create a narrative.

Who can forget the way one or two nonprofit outlets covered the Jackson water crisis a few years ago? Rather than give us the facts about a dysfunctional city government unable to maintain basic infrastructure, they used the story to feed an ideological narrative about Mississippi’s past and politics. I wish they had told us why our state capital did not have clean water.

**News as narrative has done extraordinary damage to civic discourse in this country.** It is, I am convinced, responsible for the coarsening of political debate.

So where do ordinary people go for accurate local news? Too much is presented through the prism of donor preferences. No wonder Americans often cannot agree on the facts.

I could not see a solution. Until now.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/ZhcWjLF9BHL?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
_Click on the image to read the MississippiWire.News_
| **The Mississippi Wire is a news wire, not a newspaper.** It reports, verbatim, what public officials say. It does not take what they say and press it into a narrative. It covers public bodies across the state, from the legislature down to school boards.

It is different because it is only - or almost only - primary sourced. If we quote the governor or a local official, we tell you what they said. We do not lift it to suit an editor or a partisan campaign.

That fills the void the old newspapers left, and the one the nonprofits have not been able to fill: the granular detail of truly local stories. Rather than recycle what other outlets are already saying, the Wire gives new news.

Three examples from the past fortnight. Madison County supervisors valued each Amazon data center building at $292 million. Amazon says $70 million.
Many millions of dollars of taxable value turns on who is right. Then there was the story about Jackson's public works director, who told the council his roads budget is going from $22 million to $14 million, which sounds like even bigger potholes. Or a couple of days ago in Greenville, where a judge warned about some of the unintended consequences of the new youth court law.

**The Wire lets you see what was decided, not the spin.**

A great deal of the mistrust in officials, experts and reporters has been earned. And policing speech does not fix it - we saw that during Covid. But the answer to a false narrative was never to shout it down. It is to make the record available so that anyone can check it. The Wire does not ask to be believed. It shows you what was said and lets you judge.

You can read it at MississippiWire.News. We have designed it so anyone can access the RSS feed, and we actively want other media outlets to take it. The Wire does not need to out-shout the racket. It needs to be the thing the racket gets checked against.

**We hope to set a standard for factual reporting: what officials in public bodies around the state say and decide, in their own words.**

Honest reporting. We think there is a desperate need for it.
---

Douglas Carswell

Fellow Patriot - I'm going to be straight with you, because that's the only way I know how to do this.

_We just won._ Two elections in two weeks: the special primary, then the runoff.

Grueling doesn't begin to cover it. Every dollar this campaign had went into turning out voters, running ads, and getting our message into every corner of this state.

**And it worked.**

But here's the part nobody tells you on election night: winning a runoff doesn't put a single dollar back in our account. Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes.

**Annie Andrews has $4.1 million.**

clean_body: Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes. | Fellow Patriot - I'm going to be straight with you, because that's the only way I know how to do this. We just won. Two elections in two weeks: the special primary, then the runoff. Grueling doesn't begin to cover it. Every dollar this campaign had went into turning out voters, running ads, and getting our message into every corner of this state. And it worked. But here's the part nobody tells you on election night: winning a runoff doesn't put a single dollar back in our account. Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes. Annie Andrews has $4.1 million. She's raised nearly $11 million since she got into this race, from liberal donors across the country. She's had months to build that war chest while we were fighting a two-round primary just to get our name on the November ballot. Countless conservatives in SC put their trust in me, and I promise to carry forward the conservative agenda for the next six years in the United States Senate. After asking me to run, President Trump stood on stage with me and told you why he trusts me, too. I don't intend to let a bigger bank account decide whether I get to keep that promise. The general election is November 3. That sounds far off. It isn't. It's less than 70 days away. Every week between now and then, Annie Andrews's campaign will be on television, in your mailbox, and on your phone - funded by liberal donors who wanted to defeat Lindsey and now, defeat me. We have to be able to answer that, and right now, we can't. My opponent has a $4 million head start. To catch up and rebuild, I need not only patriots who were with us over the last six weeks, but folks who are stepping up for the first time. Don't let the most radical candidate South Carolina Democrats have nominated buy this seat. Thank you for standing with me, Darline Graham United States Senator P.S.
